# Step 1: Obtain Initial Metadata from Each Project

This step sets the project directory, loads the raw SRA metadata, and optionally merges supplement tables.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

# (1) Setting working directory
project_id <- "PRJNA650272"

base_dir <- "D:/metadata_collect"
setwd(file.path(base_dir, project_id))

# (2) Loading raw SRA metadata file
sra_file <- "SraRunTable.csv"
initial_meta <- read.csv(sra_file, header = TRUE)

# (3) OPTIONAL: If extra metadata (e.g., Table.x or supplemental materials) are available from the article, you may need to merge the file with initial_meta manually. Below is example code for merging. Depending on the specific case of each study, you can customize the code as needed.
# supp_table <- read.csv("supplemental_table.csv", header = TRUE)
# initial_meta <- left_join(initial_meta, supp_table, by = merge_col_name)
```

# Step 2: Data Overview

First, you need to get an overview of the data, which includes two steps: reading the article and reading the initial metadata. This step is very IMPORTANT!

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# (1) Read the article in the following order: abstract, the beginning of the results section, and the methods. Understand the sample size, experimental design, and disease group overview. Clarify the sampling sites; for oral and gut samples, specify the exact sites like supragingival plaque, tongue, etc.

# (2) IMPORTANT: MUST go through each column of initial_meta
# head(initial_meta, 10)

# IMPORTANT: Check the unique values in the column of interest or query column.
# table(initial_meta$Assay.Type)       # WGS (30 rows) and AMPLICON (100 rows)
# table(initial_meta$Instrument)       # NextSeq 500 (WGS), Illumina MiSeq (AMPLICON)
# table(initial_meta$isolation_source) # Saliva (WGS), Gingival surface (AMPLICON)
# table(initial_meta$tissue)           # Oral (WGS), Oral gingival surface (AMPLICON)
# table(initial_meta$sex)              # "male and female" for all rows — not individually resolved
# table(initial_meta$AGE)              # "15-18" for all rows
# table(initial_meta$geo_loc_name_country)  # "uncalculated" — unusable
# table(initial_meta$Library.Name)     # subject codes: A001-A009, B001-B012, C001-C004
```

# Step 3: Removing Non-bacterial and Control Samples

First, we remove samples that do not target bacterial DNA (e.g., ITS sequencing for fungi, metatranscriptomics), then remove control and non-human samples.

```{r}
# (0) Remove non-bacterial DNA targeted samples and WGS (whole genome shotgun / metagenome)
# Check unique assay types to identify non-bacterial sequencing
unique(initial_meta$Assay.Type)
# Keep only AMPLICON (16S rRNA gene); remove WGS (whole genome shotgun), ITS, metatranscriptomics, etc.
bacterial_meta <- initial_meta[initial_meta$Assay.Type == "AMPLICON", ]
cat("Removed non-16S samples (WGS/ITS/etc.):", nrow(initial_meta) - nrow(bacterial_meta), "\n")
initial_meta <- bacterial_meta

# (1) Parameter setup
# Paper describes only human subjects (adolescent patients and healthy controls), no controls or non-human samples
control_column <- ""   # no control samples in this study
control_keywords <- c()

species_column <- "Organism"          # From initial_meta column 'Organism'
unique(initial_meta[[species_column]])
non_human_keywords <- c()             # all samples are "human oral metagenome" — no non-human samples

# (2) Remove controls and non-human samples. DO NOT need to modify code in this part, just run it.
n_samples <- nrow(initial_meta)
# Control evaluation
if (length(control_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(control_column) || control_column == "") {
    stop("Error: control_keywords provided but control_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(control_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", control_column))
  }

  control_pattern <- paste(control_keywords, collapse = "|")
  control_text <- initial_meta[[control_column]]
  is_control <- grepl(control_pattern, control_text)

} else {
  is_control <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Non-human evaluation
if (length(non_human_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(species_column) || species_column == "") {
    stop("Error: non_human_keywords provided but species_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(species_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", species_column))
  }

  non_human_pattern <- paste(non_human_keywords, collapse = "|")
  species_text <- initial_meta[[species_column]]
  is_non_human <- grepl(non_human_pattern, species_text)
} else {
  is_non_human <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Execute removal
samples_to_remove <- is_control | is_non_human
initial_meta <- initial_meta[!samples_to_remove, ]

cat("Samples after filtering bacterial DNA targets:", nrow(bacterial_meta), "\n")
cat("Removed control samples:", sum(is_control), "\n")
cat("Removed non-human samples:", sum(is_non_human), "\n")
cat("Remaining samples after Step 3:", nrow(initial_meta), "\n")
```

# Step 4: Creating a Uniform Metadata Template

This step converts the raw SRA table into the standard metadata format used in our meta-analysis.
The uniform metadata should include the following columns:
1. **bioproject**: Project ID from SRA or other database
   e.g. `PRJNA1234`, `CNP1234`, 'OEP1234', 'qiita_1234'
2. **sample_id**: SRA sample/run ID. Unique id for each sample!
   e.g. `DRR1234567`, `ERR1234567` and `SRR1234567`. If no such column exists, can use column like sample_name.
3. **subject_id**: subject id for each person if available.
   e.g. `patient_01`, `Host_03_before`, `subject12`
4. **age**: Age of the subject if available.
   e.g. `35`, `42` | not `adult`, `chilren`
5. **age_info**: If the age is not explicitly stated but approximate age range information is available, mark it in this column.
   e.g., `18-55`, `children`, `infant`, `elder`
6. **bmi**: Body Mass Index if available.
   e.g. `22.5`, `18.9` | not `normal`, `overweight`
7. **sex**: Sex of the subject.
   Mandatory to write as M/F | not `female`, `woman`
8. **sequencing_region**: Targeted 16S rRNA region.
   e.g. `V3-V4`, `V4`
9. **platform**: Sequencing platform.
   e.g. `Illumina MiSeq`, `454 GS FLX Titanium`, `Ion Torrent`
10. **country**: Country of sample origin.
    e.g. `China`, `Japan` | not city name like `Beijing`
11. **site**: Sampling site. For oral and gut sites, specify the exact sites as detailed as possible. For example, if it is known to be supragingival plaque, do not record it as 'dental plaque', unless the original text provides only a vague description.
    e.g. `saliva`, `tongue coating` | not broad term like `oral`
12. **site_group**: only accepts one of following three values: 'oral', 'gut', or 'other'.
13. **public_time**: Data release date.
    e.g. `2021-06-22` | not `June 2021`
14. **pcr_primers**: PCR primers used.
    e.g. `515F-806R`, `27F-338R` | not primer sequences
15. **title**: Title of the associated publication.
16. **disease_study**: Whether the study involves disease samples. If it's not clear, can record as NA. Only three values accepted: 'yes', 'no' or NA
17. **status**: Disease status for each sample if available, else record as NA. Only accept following abbreviations, Write full names for all other diseases.
    HC: healthy control
    CD: Crohn's disease
    CRC: colorectal cancer
    COPD: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
    HIV: human immunodeficiency virus
    ICU: intensive care unit
    OSCC: oral squamous cell carcinoma
    RA: rheumatoid arthritis
    UC: ulcerative colitis
18. **matched_samples**: Whether the subject has matched samples. Only accept 'yes' or 'no'.
19. **is_time_series**: Whether the study is a time series study. Only accept 'yes' or 'no'.

```{r}
# Extract columns from initial_meta as follows: (1) No modification needed -> extract directly. (2) Modification needed -> create a new column with the prefix raw_ and mark the original column as "pending". (3) Need to find or determine based on the article.
metadata <- data.frame(
  bioproject = initial_meta$BioProject,
  # From initial_meta column 'Run'
  sample_id = initial_meta$Run,
  # From initial_meta column 'Library Name'; subject codes embedded (e.g., A001, B003, C002)
  raw_subject_id = initial_meta$Library.Name,
  subject_id = "pending",
  # From initial_meta column 'AGE'; all rows = "15-18"
  age = NA,
  age_info = "15-18",
  bmi = NA,
  # From initial_meta column 'sex'; all rows = "male and female" — not individually resolved
  raw_sex = initial_meta$sex,
  sex = "pending",
  # From paper Methods: "hypervariable V3-V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene was PCR-amplified"
  sequencing_region = "V3-V4",
  # From paper Methods: "Illumina MiSeq" (amplicon) / "Illumina NextSeq" (WGS); set per assay type in Step 5
  platform = "pending",
  # Paper Methods: University of Szeged, Hungary. CSV geo_loc_name_country = "uncalculated" (unusable)
  country = "Hungary",
  # From initial_meta column 'isolation'; "Saliva" (WGS) or "Gingival surface" (AMPLICON)
  raw_site = initial_meta$isolate,
  site = "pending",
  site_group = "pending",
  # From initial_meta column 'ReleaseDate'
  public_time = initial_meta$ReleaseDate,
  # From paper Methods: V3-V4 primers listed in "Next generation-sequencing" paragraph
  pcr_primers = "341F-805R",
  # From paper title
  title = "Microbiomes in Supragingival Biofilms and Saliva of Adolescent Patients with Induced and Naturally Occurring Gingivitis Relative to Gingival Health",
  # Paper describes induced gingivitis, spontaneous gingivitis, and healthy controls
  disease_study = "yes",
  # Group A = induced gingivitis, Group B = spontaneous gingivitis, Group C = healthy control; status assigned in Step 5 based on Library Name prefix
  status = "pending",
  # Each subject has multiple tooth samples (4 teeth per subject)
  matched_samples = "yes",
  # Paper: single sampling per subject, no repeated measures over time
  is_time_series = "no",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
metadata$public_time <- as.Date(metadata$public_time)
```

# Step 5: Manually solving pending issues

This step involves two parts: (1) handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix, and next (2) handle the `site_group` and `matched_samples` columns.

```{r}
# (1) Handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix.

# subject_id: strip hyphen and everything after it from Library Name (e.g., "A004-13" -> "A004", "A9" -> "A9")
# From initial_meta column 'Library Name'; prefix identifies the research subject
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(subject_id = sub("-.*", "", raw_subject_id))

# sex: CSV 'sex' column is "male and female" for all rows — not individually resolved.
# Paper Methods provides group-level sex breakdown (Group A: 3M/6F, Group B: 7M/3F, Group C: 4M/5F)
# but does not map individual subjects to sex. Mark as pending since per-sample sex is unavailable.
# Individual subject-level sex cannot be determined from available data.
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(sex = NA_character_)

# site: extract from isolation_source. "Saliva" -> "saliva", "Gingival surface" -> "gingival surface"
# From initial_meta column 'isolation_source'
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(site = tolower(raw_site))

# platform: from initial_meta column 'Instrument' — Paper Methods confirms:
#   All remaining rows are AMPLICON, sequenced on "Illumina MiSeq" (MiSeq Reagent Kit v2, 500 cycles)
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(platform = "Illumina MiSeq")

# status: determine from Library Name prefix.
# Paper Methods: Group A = induced gingivitis, Group B = spontaneous gingivitis, Group C = healthy controls
# Library Name starts with A -> induced gingivitis, B -> spontaneous gingivitis, C -> healthy control
# Per template abbreviations: healthy control -> "HC"; gingivitis not in abbreviation list -> write full name
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(status = case_when(
    grepl("^A", raw_subject_id) ~ "induced gingivitis",
    grepl("^B", raw_subject_id) ~ "spontaneous gingivitis",
    grepl("^C", raw_subject_id) ~ "HC",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))
```

```{r}
# (2) Filling the 'site_group' and 'matched_samples' columns
# editing site_group
unique(metadata$site)
# All remaining samples are "gingival surface" — from paper Methods, supragingival plaque
Oral_site = c("gingival surface")
# No gut sites in this study
Gut_site = c()
# just run
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(site_group = case_when(
    site %in% Oral_site ~ "oral",
    site %in% Gut_site ~ "gut",
    TRUE ~ "other"
  ))

# editing matched_samples, just run.
# Each subject has multiple tooth samples (4 teeth per subject) -> "yes"
metadata$matched_samples <- ifelse(
  ave(metadata$subject_id, metadata$subject_id, FUN = length) > 1,
  "yes",
  "no"
)
```

```{r}
# (3) check if there is pending value in metadata. If there is pending value, go on modify the metadata.
# Function to check if a column contains "pending"
has_pending <- function(col) {
  if (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) {
    any(col == "pending", na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    FALSE
  }
}

# Check for any pending value
any_pending_value <- any(sapply(metadata, has_pending))

if (!any_pending_value) {
  message("Good! No cell contains the value 'pending'.")
} else {
  pending_cols <- names(metadata)[sapply(metadata, has_pending)]
  message("Columns containing 'pending': ", paste(pending_cols, collapse = ", "))
  message("Please continue to resolve these pending columns!")
}
```

# Step 6: Visualize the Metadata

This step makes a quick set of plots for checking the distribution of key metadata fields.

```{r}
# Select columns for visualization, just run
plot_data <- metadata %>%
  select(-bioproject, -sample_id, -subject_id, -title)

create_simple_plots <- function(data) {
  plots <- list()
  continuous_vars <- c("age", "bmi")

  for (col in colnames(data)) {
    if (all(is.na(data[[col]]))) {
      p <- ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "this column is NA", size = 6) +
        labs(title = col) +
        theme_void()
    } else if (col %in% continuous_vars && is.numeric(data[[col]])) {
      p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[col]])) +
        geom_histogram(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.6, bins = 20, na.rm = TRUE) +
        labs(title = col, x = col, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal()
    } else {
      count_data <- as.data.frame(table(data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
      p <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = reorder(Var1, -Freq), y = Freq)) +
        geom_col(fill = "red", alpha = 0.6) +
        labs(title = col, x = NULL, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
    }
    plots[[col]] <- p
  }

  return(plots)
}

# Generate and arrange plots
plots <- create_simple_plots(plot_data)
p <- plot_grid(plots$age,
               plots$age_info,
               plots$bmi,
               plots$sex,
               plots$site,
               plots$site_group,
               plots$sequencing_region,
               plots$platform,
               plots$country,
               plots$pcr_primers,
               plots$status,
               plots$matched_samples,
               ncol = 3, align = "hv", axis = "lb")
ggsave("Metadata_Summary_v2.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
# Insert Metadata_Summary_v2.png into the current Rmd output
knitr::include_graphics("Metadata_Summary_v2.png")
```

# Step 7: Sort and export the metadata

This step saves the cleaned metadata table as the final `metadata.csv` file.

```{r}
# Reorder the data frame
fixed_cols <- c("bioproject", "sample_id", "subject_id", "age", "age_info",
                "bmi", "sex", "platform", "sequencing_region", "pcr_primers",
                "country", "site", "site_group", "disease_study", "status",
                "title", "public_time", "matched_samples", "is_time_series")
metadata <- metadata %>%
  select(all_of(fixed_cols), everything())

# save metadata
# head(metadata)
write.csv(metadata, file = "metadata_v2.csv", quote = TRUE)
```
